# Repository guidance

This repository supports a UCL student research project on statistical modelling and machine learning for cybersecurity. The `Planing/` directory contains project planning material. The `wiki/` directory is the evolving, source-grounded knowledge base; its structure and content rules are defined in [wiki/README.md](../wiki/README.md) and [.github/instructions/cybersecurity-wiki.instructions.md](./instructions/cybersecurity-wiki.instructions.md).

## Working with research and the wiki

- Load the relevant cybersecurity wiki skill for source curation, cross-source synthesis, or maintenance. Keep each task within that workflow.
- Treat a user's explicit selection of a source as permission to curate it, not as permission to redistribute copyrighted material. Prefer open-access material; retain bibliographic metadata, URL, and concise notes where full-text storage is not permitted.
- Preserve captured evidence under `raw/` once recorded. Do not rewrite, move, or delete it. Do not download whole datasets into the repository; document official access routes and dataset properties instead.
- Ground substantive claims in identifiable sources. Distinguish peer-reviewed work, preprints, standards, official documentation, vendor claims, and informal discussion. Record publication and access dates when available; never invent missing facts.
- Reuse canonical pages and aliases before adding pages. Update affected cross-links, indexes, timelines, and the wiki log when those files exist.
- Do not silently merge, rename, or delete wiki pages. Flag duplicates and broken links for review; make only unambiguous repairs that preserve meaning.
- Handle cybersecurity material responsibly: prioritise defensive, reproducible research; identify dual-use implications; do not include secrets, personal data, or operational instructions that enable unauthorised access or abuse.
- Do not claim that a check, link, source status, or tool version has been verified unless it was actually checked. State limitations and unresolved questions plainly.
